correctness.rationale: Cyclic independent k-set marked gaps are uniform weak compositions of m=n-2k. Pair inclusion at separation d factors as sum of Q_d(t) Q_(n-d)(k-2-t), yielding the exact circulant covariance spectrum. A swap of an adjacent position in two valid k-sets and its cyclic translates forces all zero-variance coefficient vectors to be constant, including k=1. For fixed m, repeated defects have vanishing probability and the m single-gap defects converge to m uniform points; the near-π Fourier amplitude converges to a finite-flip random-sign integral. Squared-modulus expectation yields B_m via E[sigma(s)sigma(t)]=(1-2|s-t|)^m. At most m 00 bonds give deterministic O_m(1/|1-e^{-iδ}|) Fourier amplitude, hence uniformly summable O_m((1+|r|)^-2) intensities, proving full ℓ1 convergence, Parseval mass 1/4 and tail by integration by parts. No empirical pointwise sampling substitutes for ℓ1 domination.

value.rationale: Near-close-packed uniform independent sets of a cycle are a natural canonical combinatorial ensemble, and the whole covariance Fourier intensity is its natural diffraction/harmonic observable. The result gives a complete ℓ1 mass classification, parity-sensitive Bragg satellites, exact limiting intensity conservation, all-m tail and interpretable m=1,2 profiles, while finite covariance has one and only one null mode. This is a mathematically motivated boundary-layer theorem, not arbitrary finite-n numerics.

limitations: m is fixed positive as k tends to infinity; no growing-defect uniformity.
